sheet-2-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 2, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the western half of Laurel Springs and the edge of Stratford, between the White Horse Pike in the upper right and East Atlantic Avenue and the Atlantic City Railroad (P. & R. Ry.) along the bottom. North points to the upper left. Chestnut Avenue runs diagonally across the sheet from the pike towards the south-west, with the borough line between Laurel Springs and Stratford running beside it and then down past Almond Avenue to the railroad. South of Chestnut Avenue a grid of Trenton, Virginia, Mt. Vernon and Washington Avenues and Broadway is crossed by Central and Grand Avenues; Arch Avenue lies at the top of the Broadway blocks and Linden Avenue cuts the lower right corner. Most buildings are frame dwellings on long lots, with many blocks only partly built. Along East Atlantic Avenue near Mt. Vernon Avenue stand The Laurel Moving Picture Theatre and a steel-frame building, and the passenger station stands by the railroad at the lower right. A large public school occupies the block between Washington Avenue and Broadway south of Grand Avenue. The Laurel Springs Water Supply Co. pumping station, standpipe and wells lie between Trenton and Virginia Avenues beside a small stream, and an Electric Co. of N.J. transformer house stands on Grand Avenue. Hillcrest greenhouses stand near the pike at the top right. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along the streets, and the part is separated from part 2 (Lindenwold) by a heavy line in the upper left.
notes: Linden Avenue is now Stone Road.
Central Avenue west of Washington Avenue is now West Central Avenue.
Trenton Avenue was left out as control: the modern street runs diagonally along the old borough line, while the sheet draws it straight down the Trenton Avenue blocks.
Laurel Springs Water Supply Co. pumping station and standpipe, the public school and The Laurel Moving Picture Theatre are on this part.

100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line. Part 1 (main, lower and right): west Laurel Springs, Broadway to Almond Av, Chestnut Av to E. Atlantic Av, with Trenton, Virginia, Mt. Vernon, Washington, Central, Grand, Arch, Linden Av; Laurel Springs Water Supply Co. Part 2 (upper left): Lindenwold along White Horse Pike, South, State, Maple, Linden, Elm, Myrtle, Cooper, Irving; Lindenwold Public School. Part 2 placed from the South Av / Irving junction carried from sheet 12 part 2 plus a derived point (atlas scale, rotation -55 deg); its two White Horse Pike junctions disagree with the drawn spacing; low confidence.

sheet-2-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 2, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and set off from the rest of the sheet by a heavy line in its upper left corner, shows part of Lindenwold along the White Horse Pike, just east of the area of sheet 3. North points to the upper left, at a steeper angle than on the main part, since the part is drawn square to the White Horse Pike. The pike crosses the part from left to right; Maple Avenue and Linden Avenue cross it, with State Avenue and the end of Linden Avenue from sheet 3 in the lower left corner. North of the pike, Maple Avenue and Linden Avenue run up to South Avenue and Irving at the top edge, and Elm Avenue and Myrtle Avenue lie further east, with Cooper and an unnamed street marked not opened. The Lindenwold Public School, a heated brick-and-frame building with an annex, stands on the north side of the pike between Maple and Linden Avenues. The rest of the part is frame dwellings with sheds on deep lots, and the eastern blocks are largely empty. Water pipes of 6 inches are drawn along the pike and Linden Avenue. Sheet 12 adjoins at the top and sheet 3 on the left.
notes: Maple Avenue is now East Maple Avenue; Irving is Irving Avenue; the Linden Avenue in the lower left corner, coming from sheet 3, is now Stone Road.
Cooper and an unnamed street east of Elm Avenue are marked not opened.

The distance drawn along Maple Avenue from the White Horse Pike to South Avenue and Irving (about 660 ft) is longer than today's (about 585 ft), and the two pike junctions gave a wrong scale and rotation. The part is placed from the South Avenue / Irving / Maple Avenue junction as drawn on sheet 12 part 2, with the atlas scale and a rotation of -55 degrees read from Maple Avenue; low confidence, the pike end may be 20 m or more off.
Lindenwold Public School is on this part.

100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line. Part 1 (main, lower and right): west Laurel Springs, Broadway to Almond Av, Chestnut Av to E. Atlantic Av, with Trenton, Virginia, Mt. Vernon, Washington, Central, Grand, Arch, Linden Av; Laurel Springs Water Supply Co. Part 2 (upper left): Lindenwold along White Horse Pike, South, State, Maple, Linden, Elm, Myrtle, Cooper, Irving; Lindenwold Public School. Part 2 placed from the South Av / Irving junction carried from sheet 12 part 2 plus a derived point (atlas scale, rotation -55 deg); its two White Horse Pike junctions disagree with the drawn spacing; low confidence.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the eastern part of Laurel Springs and the adjoining western edge of Lindenwold, between the White Horse Pike along the top and East Atlantic Avenue and the Atlantic City Railroad (P. & R. Ry.) along the bottom. The sheet is turned on the page so that north points to the upper left. In Laurel Springs a regular grid runs from Broadway on the left edge through Fairmount, Madison, Hemlock and Summit Avenues, crossed by Arch, Central and Grand Avenues. Linden Avenue runs diagonally across the middle of the sheet, and the borough boundary between Laurel Springs and Lindenwold runs along it before turning south between Stafford and South Avenues to the railroad. South of Linden Avenue, Maple, Elma and Stafford Avenues run down to East Atlantic Avenue; east of the boundary the Lindenwold blocks between South, Park and Lincoln Avenues are large and lightly built, crossed by Whitman Avenue. Most buildings are frame dwellings with sheds and coops on long lots. Along the pike stand a filling station, an auto repair garage and a concrete-block garage for 30 cars, stores, and in the upper right the St. Lawrence Roman Catholic church, its parochial school and the sisters' home. The First Baptist Church faces Arch Avenue, a P.E. church and a milk depot stand in the Central and Grand Avenue blocks, the New Jersey Bell Telephone Company building stands on Broadway, and Fire Co. No. 1 stands on Maple Avenue. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches with hydrants are drawn along most streets, and several street widths (50 and 60 ft) are printed.
notes: Linden Avenue is now Stone Road.
South Avenue in the Lindenwold blocks below Linden Avenue is now Columbia Avenue; the South Avenue at the top right, near the White Horse Pike, keeps its name.
The Park Avenue below Linden Avenue is now West Park Avenue; the Park Avenue above the White Horse Pike is now East Park Avenue.
Walnut Lane (Avenue) above the pike is now Walnut Avenue, continuing Hemlock Avenue.
Summit Avenue was left out as control: the modern street lies about 30 ft (9 m) east of the drawn one.
Whitman Avenue was left out as control: its three junctions disagreed with the fit by 11 to 18 m.
The borough line between Laurel Springs and Lindenwold is drawn along Linden Avenue and the White Horse Pike.
St. Lawrence Roman Catholic Church, its parochial school and the First Baptist Church are on this sheet.

100 ft. Single part. Laurel Springs and Lindenwold between White Horse Pike and the Atlantic City R.R.: Broadway, Fairmount, Madison, Hemlock, Summit, South, Lincoln, Park, Arch, Central, Grand, Linden (now Stone Road), Maple, Elma, Stafford, Whitman, E. Atlantic Av. Pilot sheet.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, shows the south-western part of Laurel Springs, Camden County, south of the Atlantic City Railroad (P. & R. Ry.) and its West Atlantic Avenue frontage. The sheet is turned on the page so that north points to the upper left, as the compass at the top shows. A brook, here carrying the line between the Borough of Stratford and the Borough of Laurel Springs, crosses the sheet from the top centre to the lower left edge. The upper left corner is the Stratford side, with Brazil Avenue running across it, a few scattered dwellings and the railroad lines and a 6 inch water pipe along the top edge. The main business frontage is in the upper right, along West Atlantic Avenue, where the Laurel Springs National Bank, a garage, stores and a tin and plumbing shop stand together. A diagonal street, Stone Road, also lettered (W. Elm), crosses the middle of the sheet and passes the Laurel Springs Fire Company No. 2 and a printing works (Louis Fink and Son, printers). South of it, a regular grid of Walnut, Beech, Glen and Park Avenues runs down to Lakeview Avenue, crossed by Locust Avenue. Blocks are lined with narrow numbered lots, mostly with frame dwellings, coops and sheds, and some lots are empty. A Presbyterian church stands in the block east of Park Avenue. Tomlinson Avenue closes the sheet on the right. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches with hydrants are drawn in most streets, and several street widths (50 and 60 ft) are printed. Sheets 2, 5, 6 and 10 adjoin.
notes: Stone Road (West Elm) is the street drawn as Linden Avenue on sheets 2 and 3; it is Stone Road today.
Laurel Avenue is now Laurel Road.
Locust Avenue west of Beech Avenue is now East Locust Avenue.

100 ft. Single part. Laurel Springs south of the Atlantic City R.R.: Stone Rd (W. Elm), Walnut, Beech, Glen, Park, Tomlinson, Locust, Lakeview, W. Atlantic; brook (Stratford/Laurel Springs line) in the NW; Brazil Av at the top left.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the eastern and southern parts of Laurel Springs and the adjoining Lindenwold shore of Laurel Lake. The sheet is turned on the page so that north points to the upper left. The Atlantic City Railroad (P. & R. Ry.) crosses the top right with West Atlantic Avenue and East Atlantic Avenue on either side of it. South of the tracks a regular grid of Tomlinson, Lindsey, Maple, Elma and Stafford Avenues is cut by Poplar and Lakeview Avenues; the blocks hold frame dwellings, coops and sheds on long numbered lots, with an auto repair shop at Lindsey Avenue and the Crystal Inn, a summer boarding house, near Maple Avenue. A wooden bridge is lettered beside Maple Avenue at the railroad. At the upper right the borough line between Laurel Springs and Lindenwold runs down between Stafford and South Avenues, and the Eagles Hall stands on the Lindenwold side. In the lower half Laurel Lake and its inflow, Trout Run, take up much of the sheet; the borough boundary follows the lake and the run. Below the lake the sheet shows Lindenwold, with the subdivided strips of Laurel Landing on the lake shore at the left and, at the bottom, Lake Boulevard, Scott, Columbia and Cottage Avenues and 1st, 2nd and Wade Avenues, laid out in narrow lots with few buildings. The De Soto Country Club building and a second structure stand at the right edge. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and many street widths (30, 40, 50 and 60 ft) are printed. Sheets 3, 4, 6 and 8 adjoin.
notes: Lindsey Avenue is now Lindsay Avenue; Maple, Elma and Stafford Avenues here are West Maple, West Elma and West Stafford Avenues.
South Avenue on this sheet is Columbia Avenue today.

1st Avenue, Columbia Avenue, Wade Avenue and Lake Boulevard in the lower right were left out as control: their modern lines do not match the drawn spacing (drawn about 950 px between Lake Boulevard, 1st and Wade Avenues, modern about 840 px).

100 ft. Single part. Poplar, Lakeview, Tomlinson, Lindsey, Maple, Elma, Stafford, South Av; Laurel Lake and Trout Run; Lindenwold below the lake (Lake Blvd, Scott, Columbia, Cottage, 1st, 2nd, Wade). Lower third has no control (1st, Wade, Scott, Lake Blvd left out: modern spacing does not match the drawn).

sheet-6-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 6, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers Laurel Lake and the streets on both its shores, between Laurel Avenue on the left edge and Tomlinson Avenue on the right. North points to the upper left, at a smaller angle than on sheets 2 and 3. On the Laurel Springs shore, Lakeview Avenue along the top and Sycamore Avenue are crossed by Walnut, Beech, Glen and Park Avenues; the blocks hold frame dwellings, a filling station and a windmill with tower at Laurel Avenue, and the Laurel Springs Country Club on the lake shore at Walnut Avenue. A brook in a gully runs down from Lakeview Avenue between Glen and Park Avenues, and boat houses and a pavilion stand at the edge of the bluff at Tomlinson Avenue. Laurel Avenue crosses the lake's outlet on an iron bridge at the left edge. The borough line between Laurel Springs and Lindenwold follows the lake. On the Lindenwold shore the lake front is cut into narrow lots served by footways and landings: Grove Landing, The Ramble, Lake Walk, Bluff Walk, Neptune Walk and Mermaid Walk, Terrace Landing, Manor Landing and Spring Landing, with Bermick Park, all running down to Lake Boulevard. The stubs of Woodland, Clover, Homesite and Central Avenues and 2nd Avenue leave Lake Boulevard towards sheet 7. Few buildings stand on the Lindenwold side. The lower right of the sheet is blank, and the lower left is a separate part (part 2).
notes: Laurel Avenue is now Laurel Road.
Lake Boulevard was left out as control: the modern road lies north of the drawn one for most of its length.
All control points are on Lakeview and Sycamore Avenues, north of the lake; the Lindenwold shore is placed by extrapolation.
Sycamore Avenue is marked not open west of Walnut Avenue.
Laurel Springs Country Club is on this part.

100 ft. Two parts. Part 1 (main): Laurel Lake from Laurel Av east to Tomlinson Av, Lakeview and Sycamore Av, Lake Blvd and the landings of Lindenwold (Grove, Terrace, Manor, Spring Landing). Part 2 (lower left, heavy line): strip west of Laurel Av from Sycamore Av south across the North Branch of Timber Creek, Margaret Y. Stone Memorial Home and a grist mill, drawn displaced at the same rotation. Part 2 placed from part 1 (iron bridge carried, plus a derived point); low confidence.

sheet-6-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 6, drawn at 100 ft to an inch in a box at the lower left of the sheet, shows the strip of ground on the west side of Laurel Avenue from Sycamore Avenue south across the North Branch of Timber Creek. It lies immediately west of the left edge of part 1 and is drawn at the same rotation, shifted down and to the right on the page. Laurel Avenue runs down the right side of the box, with the borough line between Stratford and Laurel Springs along it; Sycamore Avenue is marked at the top right corner. In the upper part of the box, in Stratford, stand the Margaret Y. Stone Memorial Home, a brick and frame building, with a feed store, coops and sheds. Further south the North Branch of Timber Creek leaves Laurel Lake under the iron bridge of Laurel Avenue; the creek carries the borough line between Stratford and Lindenwold. A raceway and an underground flume lead from a gate at the bridge to a grist mill driven by water power, and a few frame dwellings stand below it in Lindenwold. The rest of the box is open ground, marked no exposure along its top and bottom edges.
notes: Laurel Avenue is now Laurel Road.

Placed from part 1 on the assumption that the box is part 1's ground shifted on the page: one point at the iron bridge, drawn on both parts, and one derived point 300 ft up Laurel Avenue; low confidence.
The Margaret Y. Stone Memorial Home and a water-powered grist mill are on this part.

100 ft. Two parts. Part 1 (main): Laurel Lake from Laurel Av east to Tomlinson Av, Lakeview and Sycamore Av, Lake Blvd and the landings of Lindenwold (Grove, Terrace, Manor, Spring Landing). Part 2 (lower left, heavy line): strip west of Laurel Av from Sycamore Av south across the North Branch of Timber Creek, Margaret Y. Stone Memorial Home and a grist mill, drawn displaced at the same rotation. Part 2 placed from part 1 (iron bridge carried, plus a derived point); low confidence.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers a planned residential tract of Lindenwold south of Lake Boulevard and the shore of Laurel Lake, bounded on the left by Laurel Avenue and at the bottom by Chews Landing Road. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left. The ground is divided into a rectangular grid of long blocks by Woodland, Clover, Homesite and Central Avenues running down the sheet and the numbered avenues, 3rd to 10th, running across it. Nearly every block is cut into narrow numbered lots, 25 ft or so wide, and most of them are still empty; frame dwellings with sheds and coops are scattered in the blocks near the middle and right, and a few stand on the Laurel Avenue frontage on the left. Some blocks are broken by a 50 ft wide strip. In the top left corner a group of short walks (Neptune Walk, Mermaid Walk) and lake landings (Terrace Landing, Manor Landing) lead down from the lake, and Lake Boulevard curves across the top of the sheet. The map-edge note on the left margin reads vacant beyond Laurel Avenue. A 4 inch water pipe is drawn in the 5th Avenue line at the left, and a 4 inch pipe is lettered at the right edge. The title cartouche of Laurel Springs, N.J., with Lindenwold written beneath, is at the top. Sheets 6 and 8 adjoin on the north and east, and the numbered blocks (125 to 174) are the Sanborn block numbers of this part of the borough.
notes: Laurel Avenue is now Laurel Road.
Lake Boulevard was left out as control: the modern road lies north of the drawn one.
100 ft. Single part. Lindenwold: Woodland, Clover, Homesite, Central, 3rd to 10th Av, Chews Landing Rd, Laurel Av on the left; lake walks and landings at the top.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, continues the Lindenwold tract of sheet 7 to the east, from 2nd Avenue at the top to Chews Landing Road at the bottom. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left. On the left, Cottage, Elm and Scott Avenues cross the numbered avenues, 2nd to 10th, in long blocks cut into narrow lots; Elm Avenue is a short street that only opens out between 6th and 7th Avenues. Scott Avenue is 50 ft wide, and the lots along its east side run out as narrow strips. Buildings are few: frame dwellings and sheds scattered through the blocks, the Fire Department of No. 2 Company, Lindenwold, on Scott Avenue near 4th Avenue, and the Garden Lake Public School in the block at the lower left. East of Scott Avenue the large empty blocks are crossed by Wright Avenue, and beyond them the streets turn to a different angle: Columbia Avenue and a 50 ft wide road run down the right side, with 2nd to 6th Avenues set off them in short blocks of long thin lots, and Park Avenue continuing south as a diagonal road. Pine Grove Avenue, Miller Avenue and Central Avenue bound the sparsely built blocks at the lower right. A compass and the title cartouche (Laurel Springs, N.J., Lindenwold) fill the upper right. Sheets 5, 7 and 9 adjoin.
notes: Park Avenue here is West Park Avenue today.
Columbia Avenue / Wade Avenue and Miller Avenue / West Park Avenue were excluded as control (residuals of about 5 m).
A 6 inch water pipe is drawn in Chews Landing Road.
100 ft. Single part. Lindenwold: Cottage, Elm, Scott, Wright, Columbia, Park, Pine Grove, Miller, Central, 2nd to 10th Av; east part drawn at a different street angle, no dividing line.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, shows the Borough of Stratford between Kirkwood Avenue at the top and the Atlantic City Railroad (P. & R. Ry.) with East and West Atlantic Avenues at the bottom. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left; the compass is at the top. Six parallel streets named after colleges, Columbia, Cornell, Vassar, Yale, Harvard and Princeton Avenues, cross Kirkwood, Central and Grand Avenues in a regular grid of 50 ft streets. The western two thirds of the sheet is laid out in large numbered blocks (6 to 9, 22 to 25) with no buildings on them at all. Houses, sheds and coops are concentrated in the eastern blocks between Yale and Princeton Avenues, with a few on the Vassar Avenue blocks near Grand Avenue. The Old Orchard Inn, with its spring house, stands near Harvard Avenue north of Grand Avenue, and a poultry house and several frame dwellings stand in the blocks near Kirkwood Avenue. Along the bottom the three-track railroad lies between East Atlantic Avenue and West Atlantic Avenue; a coal yard (R. C. Parker Coal Co.), coal bins and a plumbing shop stand beside it. A dash-dot line marks the borough limits and the name Clementon Township appears beyond it at the lower left. The title cartouche reads Laurel Springs, N.J., with Stratford beneath it. 6 inch water pipes are drawn in some streets. Sheets 4, 10 and 11 adjoin.
notes: Kirkwood Avenue west of Yale Avenue is North Kirkwood Avenue today.
East Atlantic Avenue here is North Atlantic Avenue today.
Grand Avenue west of Cornell Avenue is North Grand Avenue today.
100 ft. Single part. Stratford: Columbia to Princeton Av between Kirkwood and E./W. Atlantic; western two thirds empty blocks.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, shows the built-up centre of the Borough of Stratford, east of the area of sheet 9, from Kirkwood Avenue at the top to the Atlantic City Railroad at the bottom. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left, as the compass at the upper right shows. Princeton, Union, Jefferson and Oxford Avenues run down the sheet and cross Kirkwood, Central and Grand Avenues; Laurel Avenue runs diagonally down the right side, with long narrow lots laid out along its west side. The blocks hold a close pattern of frame dwellings with coops and sheds on numbered lots, with the Stratford M. E. Church on Central Avenue near Union Avenue, and a few buildings, some of them large, stand beyond Laurel Avenue at the top. At the bottom the P. & R. Ry. passenger station and a post office stand on East Atlantic Avenue, and the three-track railroad runs along the sheet, with West Atlantic Avenue beyond it. Below the tracks the sheet is mostly empty: Swathmore Avenue and Pennsylvania Avenue are drawn across large vacant blocks. The whole upper right quarter of the sheet is blank paper, carrying only block and sheet numbers (40, 2, 4) of the neighbouring parts of the atlas, and a dash-dot line near the right edge. Water pipes of 6 inches with hydrants are drawn in most streets, with a pipe lettered to Laurel Springs along East Atlantic Avenue. Sheets 9, 11 and 4 adjoin.
notes: Laurel Avenue is now Laurel Road East, and Swathmore Avenue is Swarthmore Avenue on today's map.
Laurel Road East and Pennsylvania Avenue junctions were excluded as control (residuals of 4 to 8 m).

100 ft. Single part. Stratford centre: Princeton, Union, Jefferson, Oxford, Laurel Av diagonal, Kirkwood, Central, Grand, E./W. Atlantic, Swathmore, Pennsylvania; NE quarter blank; weak control south of the tracks.

sheet-11-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 11, drawn at 100 ft to an inch across the top half of the sheet, covers the centre of Stratford between the White Horse Pike and Kirkwood Avenue. North points to the upper left. The pike crosses the part near the top, with the line between Clementon Township to the north and the Borough of Stratford to the south drawn along it, and Old Shore Road branching off at the top right. The college-named avenues cross it from left to right: Columbia, Cornell, Lafayette, Vassar, Yale, Harvard and Princeton Avenues; Cornell and Vassar Avenues are offset where they cross the pike, and Cornell and Vassar Avenues are marked not opened south of it. North of the pike the Somerdale Inn, filling stations, a row of stores and The White Horse Hotel face the road. South of it stand the H. R. Nicholson garage with an auto shop and repair shop, the American Legion building, and a public school of fireproof construction between Harvard and Princeton Avenues, with frame dwellings and a group of brick-veneer houses on Columbia Avenue. The large blocks between Columbia and Vassar Avenues are mostly empty. A row of empty blocks south of Kirkwood Avenue, marked with the number of sheet 9, closes the part at the heavy line across the middle of the sheet.
notes: Kirkwood Avenue west of Yale Avenue is now North Kirkwood Avenue; its junctions there were left out as control (Columbia Avenue about 11 m off the fit).
The White Horse Pike is a divided road here today; both carriageway junctions of Cornell Avenue were used, matching the offset crossings drawn.
Cornell Avenue and Vassar Avenue are marked not opened south of the pike.
The Somerdale Inn, The White Horse Hotel, the American Legion building and the public school are on this part.

100 ft. Three parts split by heavy lines. Part 1 (top): Stratford, White Horse Pike to Kirkwood Av, Columbia to Princeton Av. Part 2 (middle and lower left): White Horse Pike, Old Shore Rd, Blackwood & Moorestown Rd, Princeton, Union, Laurel, Kirkwood Av. Part 3 (lower right box): White Horse Pike at Arlington Av, Clementon Twp. Part 3 anchored on Arlington Av / White Horse Pike (scale assumed); low confidence.

sheet-11-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 11, drawn at 100 ft to an inch between the two heavy lines of the sheet and in its lower left corner, covers the east end of Stratford along the White Horse Pike. North points to the upper left. Old Shore Road runs diagonally across the top, with the line between Clementon Township and the Borough of Stratford, and further east the Borough of Lindenwold, drawn along it. Blackwood & Moorestown Road crosses it and the pike and continues south as Union Avenue. The White Horse Pike crosses the whole width of the part, lined on both sides by numbered lots with a few dwellings, stores, a hay storage and a flour and feed store, and a kennels. Below the pike, Princeton Avenue runs down the left edge and Laurel Avenue branches diagonally from Union Avenue towards Kirkwood Avenue at the bottom edge. The Stratford Fire Dept. Co. No. 1 stands on Union Avenue, and the blocks between the avenues hold frame dwellings and garages. The large block east of Old Shore Road and Blackwood & Moorestown Road is almost empty. The lower right of the sheet is a separate part (part 3).
notes: Laurel Avenue is now Laurel Road East.
Placed from four junctions only (Princeton Avenue at the pike, and Kirkwood Avenue at Princeton, Union and Laurel Avenues).
Stratford Fire Dept. Co. No. 1 is on this part.

100 ft. Three parts split by heavy lines. Part 1 (top): Stratford, White Horse Pike to Kirkwood Av, Columbia to Princeton Av. Part 2 (middle and lower left): White Horse Pike, Old Shore Rd, Blackwood & Moorestown Rd, Princeton, Union, Laurel, Kirkwood Av. Part 3 (lower right box): White Horse Pike at Arlington Av, Clementon Twp. Part 3 anchored on Arlington Av / White Horse Pike (scale assumed); low confidence.

sheet-11-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 11, drawn at 100 ft to an inch in a box at the lower right of the sheet, shows the White Horse Pike where Arlington Avenue leaves it, on the edge of Stratford. North points to the upper left, as on the rest of the sheet. The pike runs across the bottom of the box, curving slightly, and Arlington Avenue runs up from it towards the top edge, which is marked no exposure. A concrete-block garage for 25 cars with cement floor, electric lights and steam heat stands on the north side of the pike west of Arlington Avenue, and a few frame dwellings and a store stand on Arlington Avenue and along the pike. A 4-inch water pipe runs up Arlington Avenue. Most of the box is empty ground.
notes: Placed from one measured junction (Arlington Avenue at the White Horse Pike), with the scale assumed from the rest of the atlas and the rotation from the measured lines; low confidence.

sheet-12-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 12, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the northern part of Lindenwold on both sides of the Pennsylvania Railroad (West Jersey & Seashore Division), whose double track crosses the sheet a quarter of the way down. North points to the upper left. North of the railroad, Bryant along the top and Carlton beside the tracks are crossed by Locust, Walnut, Maple and Linden Avenues; these blocks are laid out in lots but hold only a few dwellings. South of the railroad, Berlin Avenue runs beside the tracks, and Shadyside, Highland, Locust, Walnut, Maple and Linden Avenues run down to Hawthorne, Emerson and Lowell. The blocks between Walnut and Linden Avenues are the most built up, with frame dwellings, garages and a few stores, while the western blocks between Shadyside and Locust Avenues are partly built and the large block 231 in the lower middle is almost empty. Walnut Lane runs diagonally across the lower part of the sheet from Emerson towards the south-west, with an unopened street beside it. The boundary between the Borough of Lindenwold and the Borough of Stratford crosses the open ground at the left edge. The lower left corner of the sheet is a separate part (part 2).
notes: Bryant is now Bryant Street; Carlton is North Carlton Street; Berlin Avenue is Berlin Road North; Hawthorne is Hawthorne Street; Emerson is Emerson Street; Lowell is East Lowell Street.
Maple Avenue and Linden Avenue are now East Maple Avenue and East Linden Avenue.
Walnut Lane is now part of Walnut Avenue, which runs diagonally to Emerson Street and East Maple Avenue.
The two crossings of the railroad (now the Atlantic City Line) were rejected as control (3.5 m off the street fit).

100 ft. Two parts. Part 1 (main): Lindenwold, Bryant and Carlton north of the P.R.R. (W.J.& S.S. Divn), Berlin Av, Shadyside, Highland, Locust, Walnut, Maple, Linden Av, Hawthorne, Emerson, Lowell, Walnut Lane. Part 2 (lower left box): Lowell to South Av and Irving, Maple, Linden, Elm Av.

sheet-12-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 12, drawn at 100 ft to an inch in a box at the lower left of the sheet, continues the Lindenwold streets of part 1 southwards from Lowell to South Avenue and Irving. It is drawn at the same rotation as part 1, shifted on the page, with north to the upper left. Maple Avenue, Linden Avenue and Elm Avenue run down the box from Lowell at the top to South Avenue and Irving at the bottom; a row of lots west of Maple Avenue is drawn along the left edge. The blocks hold frame dwellings with sheds and garages on narrow lots, more densely built on Linden Avenue and Elm Avenue than further west. Below South Avenue and Irving the box shows the tops of the next blocks, which belong to sheet 2. Water pipes are drawn along Linden Avenue.
notes: Lowell is now East Lowell Street (South Lowell Avenue east of Linden); Maple Avenue and Linden Avenue are East Maple Avenue and East Linden Avenue; Irving is Irving Avenue.
Placed from four junctions at its corners.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, shows the central part of Lindenwold on the Pennsylvania Railroad (W. J. & S. S. Division) line, east of sheet 12 and bounded by Linden Avenue on the left. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left. The railroad crosses the upper third of the sheet from left to right, with Carlton lettered along its north side and Berlin Avenue along the south side; a spur and the Lindenwold station stand at the left. North of the tracks, Bryant at the top and the numbered lots between Bryant and Carlton are mostly vacant: several streets there are marked Not Open, and the Lindenwold Congregational Church and a few frame dwellings stand on the Linden Avenue side. In the upper right, 3rd Street and 2nd Street cross a block of lots near Central Avenue, beside the title cartouche (Laurel Springs, N.J., with Lindenwold beneath) and a compass. South of the tracks a regular grid of long blocks (numbers 225 to 247) is laid out by Linden, Elm, Myrtle, Cedar, Chestnut and Spruce Avenues crossing Hawthorne, Emerson and Lowell. Houses are concentrated along Berlin Avenue and Hawthorne, with a fire department hall and a hall at the corner of Linden Avenue and Berlin Avenue; the lower blocks have only a few buildings, mainly at the left. Lot numbers and 50 ft street widths are marked throughout. Sheet 12 adjoins on the left and below, as the number 12 beside Linden Avenue and at the foot of the sheet shows.
notes: Bryant, Carlton, Hawthorne, Emerson and Lowell are Bryant Street, North Carlton Street, Hawthorne Street, Emerson Street and East Lowell Street today; Hawthorne east of Myrtle Avenue is South Hawthorne Avenue and Lowell east of Myrtle Avenue is South Lowell Avenue.
Linden Avenue is East Linden Avenue today, Elm Avenue is East Elm Avenue, and Berlin Avenue is Berlin Road North.
Norcross Avenue and the streets between Bryant and Carlton are not in OpenStreetMap; several are marked Not Open on the sheet.
South Carlton Street junctions at Elm and Myrtle Avenues were left out as control (residuals of 3 m and more beside the railroad).

100 ft. Single part. Lindenwold along the P.R.R. (W.J.&S.S. Divn): Bryant, Carlton, Berlin Av, Hawthorne, Emerson, Lowell, Linden, Elm, Myrtle, Norcross, Cedar, Chestnut, Spruce, Central, 2nd and 3rd St.
